publication_fingerprints.headline: The Dog Stars
publication_fingerprints.event_text:
The Dog Stars Rohan Naahar is a News Writer for Collider. From Francois Ozon to David Fincher, he'll watch anything once.
He has covered everything from Marvel to the Oscars, and Marvel at the Oscars. He also writes obsessively about the box office, charting the many hits and misses that are released weekly, and how their commercial performance shapes public perception. In his time at Collider, he has also helped drive diversity by writing stories about the multiple Indian film industries, with a goal of introducing audiences to a whole new world of cinema.
Director Ridley Scott's long-awaited return to the sci-fi genre with The Dog Stars didn't exactly go according to plan. The movie underperformed in its box-office debut and received mediocre reviews. It had been nearly a decade since Scott made a sci-fi movie; his previous release was Alien: Covenant, which fell short of box-office expectations as well and sent its iconic franchise into hibernation for several years. The Alien series was resurrected by Fede Álvarez's Alien: Romulus, which grossed $350 million worldwide and received an 80% score on the aggregator website Rotten Tomatoes. Scott wasn't quite impressed, however. In a recent inter Ridley Scott's sci‑fi film The Dog Stars is now available to stream on Peacock. Added to Peacock library Box‑office underperformed Scott plans a sequel to Alien: Covenant Peacock

IT: Welcome to Derry When it was first announced that Stephen King's novel It, which had already been adapted into a miniseries and two movies, was returning again as a prequel series on HBO Max, it felt like an unnecessary cash grab. Sure, Bill Skarsgård was returning, along with creatives Andy Muschietti and Barbara Muschietti, but what could be gained by having Pennywise chase a new group of kids?
Despite the odds, IT: Welcome to Derry is a fun and terrifying show, one that takes its time building up to the killer clown. It also finds its reason to exist by exploring storylines only briefly mentioned in King's original novel. IT: Welcome to Derry has been confirmed to return for a second season, and when it does, the story will jump backward to an era that will turn the series into something more akin to Boardwalk Empire or Peaky Blinders.
What Will 'IT: Welcome to Derry' Season 2 Be About?
Pennywise, while appearing as a scary-as-hell clown, is no mortal human. Instead, the clown is merely one form taken by an extraterrestrial creature that has fed on fear for thousands of years, returning every 27 years to find more victims. publication_fingerprints.event_text:
The Spiral The Venice Film Festival has a new guilty pleasure.
The hometown crowd went wild Monday night for the world premiere of The Spiral, a campy, fun Italian horror thriller from director Paolo Strippoli (The Holy Boy, A Classic Horror Story).
Jasmine Trinca (Saint Laurent, The Caiman) stars as Anna, a controlling mother who makes a deal with the devil, in the form of a trench coat-wearing, chain-smoking Valeria Bruni Tedeschi, to save her daughter Alice (Romana Maggiora Vergano) after a gruesome accident. But the agreement sets off a, you guessed it, spiral of macabre events that will end up tearing the family apart. Adriano Giannini plays Anna’s wealthy alpha-male businessman husband, Walter. Andrea Genovese plays their son Tobia.
The twisty genre film, which dips into Grand Guignol territory, with plenty of OTT performances — led by Tedeschi’s glorious turn — may be an outsider for the Golden Lion, but it definitely played for the Venice audience, which gave it a warm and enthusiastic standing ovation, with the director and cast coaxing the crowd to keep clapping past the 9-minute mark.

The Good Place After plenty of speculation, we’ve now got official confirmation that The Good Place is leaving Netflix in all regions where it carries the “Netflix Original” branding on September 25th, just as we previously covered back here when the United States saw the series depart in full.
If you’ve logged onto X (formerly Twitter), Reddit, or TikTok recently, you’ve probably seen the outrage and confusion from subscribers. The prevailing question we’re seeing in our inboxes is: “Wait, how can Netflix remove a Netflix Original?!”
"Only on Netflix"
"Leaving soon"
Then where the fuck do I watch it? pic.twitter.com/IY49bL7HI3
— Sponge ! ⛓️🪚👱 era (@SussedSponge) September 6, 2026
It’s a valid question. After all, the word “Original” implies that Netflix made it, owns it, and will keep it on its servers until the end of time. But the reality of streaming rights is a lot more complicated than a red ‘N’ logo on a thumbnail.
Here’s the scoop on why Eleanor, Chidi, Tahani, and Jason are packing their bags, and why “Original” doesn’t always mean forever.
The “Netflix Original” Label Explained
To understand why The Good Place is leaving, we have to look back at how the show was distributed.

publication_fingerprints.headline: Untold: Raygun: Breaking Badly
publication_fingerprints.event_text:
Untold: Raygun: Breaking Badly The latest entry in the Untold documentary series, Raygun: Breaking Badly, offers a new kind of story. The 72‑minute doc tells the tale of Olympian Dr. Rachael Gunn—the PhD‑holding breakdancer from Australia who became a viral sensation for her catastrophic shutout (an iconic 0‑point run) during the Paris 2024 Olympics. Some see her as a fearless force to be reckoned with; others view her as a farce and an embarrassment to her country. But now, after the land‑down‑under dancer went down under, she got to tell her story from her perspective. But what did the doc reveal that wasn’t already widely known about the kangaroo‑hopping, sprinkler‑spreading breakdancer?
She got into breakdancing through her husband, a Breakin' fan.
Gunn met her husband Sam Free (aka emcee Sammy Sex) in 2008. He was always enthralled by the ’80s movie Breakin’ and, like the protagonist Kelly, made breakdancing his entire personality. Unlike every other woman he dated, when Samuel showed Rachael his world, she didn’t run in the opposite direction. Instead, she fell in love with it—mostly because of its gender intersectionality.
Australia doesn't have much of a B‑girl scene.

Released theatrically back in April by Focus Features, the documentary is directed by Academy Award winner Morgan Neville, the acclaimed filmmaker behind Won’t You Be My Neighbor?, 20 Feet From Stardom, and Piece by Piece , plus some other titles you’ve seen on Netflix as of late, including Saint of Second Chances and Breakdown: 1975.
Rather than a dry, encyclopedic history of SNL, Lorne takes a sprightly, entertaining approach to uncovering the notoriously elusive television titan. Since Michaels himself is famously hard to pin down, Neville relies on a massive, star-studded roster of comedy legends and SNL alumni to fill in the gaps.
Throughout the film’s 101-minute runtime, you’ll see interviews and appearances from the likes of Tina Fey, Maya Rudolph, Jimmy Fallon, Seth Meyers, Conan O’Brien, Simple Martin, Chris Rock, Colin Jost, Kristen Wiig, and even Michaels’ close friend, Paul Simon.

Crew Girl For fans of YA dramas, Netflix has your next binge lined up. Introducing Crew Girl, a new 8-episode series about a rowing-mad teen girl who finds herself coxswaining a crew of eight boys. Here’s our big interview with executive producer Jeff Norton to tell you how the project came together.
Between working on Geek Girl, being the showrunner of Finding Her Edge, and helping bring Netflix’s latest YA drama Crew Girl to our screens as an executive producer, Jeff Norton is a busy man nowadays. As we began our interview over Zoom, he was sitting in the passenger seat of a car, traveling between sets while filming the new season of Finding Her Edge. We spoke to him about what we can expect from Finding Her Edge Season 2 in more detail here. In this interview, we discuss how his latest project, Crew Girl, came together.
In Crew Girl, we follow 16-year-old rowing prodigy Teagan Tao (Miku Martineau), who, after a family scandal, is forced to move to a new school on the other side of the country with her mother. Zoltar Filming is well underway for Netflix’s upcoming star-studded Roald Dahl series, currently filming under the working title of Zoltar, and we’ve got some brand new behind-the-scenes looks at the cast in action on location in the North of England.
As we previously reported back in August exclusively, Netflix is bringing a brand new serialized adaptation of Roald Dahl’s iconic adult short stories to our screens. Think Tales of the Unexpected, but with a fresh, modern, and delightfully twisted spin from writer and executive producer Danny Brocklehurst (Fool Me Once, Run Away).
The project was officially confirmed by Netflix just recently when they unveiled their massive UK slate at the Edinburgh TV Festival. Now, we’ve obtained some additional behind-the-scenes snaps of the sprawling ensemble cast hard at work, and it could reveal that the same cast will be across the full season, meaning that while it’s likely an anthology, season 1 will see the same characters throughout as one story and, presumably, future seasons adapting other stories.
As we previously covered, we’re expecting this to be adapting the short story: Lamb to the Slaughter, with Coughlan playing Mary Malony.

The company, which is based in New York and London, will look to provide institutional capital and media and finance expertise to premium indie film and television projects in the $5-$15M range.
With a focus on English-language projects, the platform will provide flexible, structured capital to projects and production companies “with strong creative, commercial and distribution fundamentals.”
The company has said it will look to finance production, distribution and eventually MGs, P&A, tax credit facilities, presale advances, gap financing and remaining rights structures. Total value of the fund was not disclosed.

publication_fingerprints.headline: Disney+
publication_fingerprints.event_text:
Disney+ Disney Australia and New Zealand delivered its 2026 Upfronts in Melbourne on Thursday, where Disney+ was the shining centrepiece.
The company delivered a straightforward message for media buyers: audiences may watch alone, but the biggest streaming moments are still shared, discussed, and, ideally, advertised around.
“Few companies bring storytelling, technology and fandom together the way Disney can,” Kylie Watson-Wheeler, senior vice president and managing director of The Walt Disney Company Australia and New Zealand and head of ESPN Asia-Pacific, said.
“That makes Disney+ an unmatched launchpad for advertisers seeking cultural impact in premium, trusted environments.”
Disney repeatedly returned to the idea that the “future of streaming is shared”.
That does not mean everyone is suddenly piling onto the same couch. Instead, the viewing experience continues after the credits, as finales are picked apart online and new series become fodder for the group chat.
Disney wants brands to sit alongside the shows, events and franchises audiences are already discussing, particularly as the company heads into the busy holiday release period.

You can find our previous filming dates dump for Summer 2026 here.
Important: All filming dates (start and end) are subject to change due to the complexity of productions. This is also based on intel that we’ve obtained and verified to the best of our ability.

publication_fingerprints.event_text:
A Magnificent Life The master of hand-drawn animation is making his way to your Netflix queue. Sylvain Chomet’s beautifully crafted animated feature, A Magnificent Life, is officially set to make its SVOD debut, arriving on Netflix in the United States on Thursday, September 24th, 2026.
Following its world premiere at the 2025 Cannes Film Festival and a US theatrical run this past spring via Sony Pictures Classics, the acclaimed film is the latest highly anticipated title to arrive on Netflix as part of the streamer’s ongoing Pay-1 window deal with Sony.
September is turning out to be an absolute powerhouse month for fresh third-party movie pickups. A Magnificent Life joins a remarkably diverse and stacked lineup of recent SVOD premieres hitting Netflix US. It follows the award-winning Iraqi drama The President’s Cake (which dropped earlier on September 3rd), the extreme sports documentary Girl Climber (September 16th), the campy Bleecker Street disaster spoof Stop! That! Train! (September 20th), and the British cyber-heist thriller LifeHack (September 23rd).
Here is everything you need to know about this gorgeous new addition before it drops on Netflix.
What is A Magnificent Life about?

Lupin “We have a new Lupin.”
These shocking words are uttered at the start of the trailer for Netflix‘s highly anticipated Lupin Part 4, which launches October 23.
With the titular character stuck in a glass box, another appears to be on the loose, and the police are keen to find them. Throughout the trailer, we see Assane up to his own tricks, donning different disguises and sewing confusion along the way.
Lupin Part 4 begins four years after the end of the previous part. Assane wants to serve out his sentence and keep the promise he made to his son to go and meet their family in Senegal. But his plans are turned upside down by a mysterious announcement signed by Lupin, that multiple museums are to be hit with simultaneous heists.
Omar Sy will of course return to reprise his iconic role, which has turned Lupin into one of Netflix’s top non-English language shows of all time, and one of its biggest even if you include English language fare.

The Spread, headlined and executive produced by Oscar winner Javier Bardem, hails from Ozark co-creator Bill Dubuque, Sean Sansiveri and Fifth Season, with Kingsman helmer Matthew Vaughn set to direct.
The indie studio defied convention by taking the project out in August, usually considered a dead period with many executives on vacation as the TV business takes a breather before an expected post-Labor Day influx of pitches.
The timing proved fortuitous as The Spread sparked a lot of interest that translated into meetings and ultimately offers. According to sources, Netflix, Prime Video, Paramount+ and Apple TV all came in strong with offers that included a mix of writers rooms and straight-to-series orders. The bids were raised as the process went along, including a potential two-season pickup, I hear.
Watch on Deadline
Word is that the two major streamers overseen by former Netflix executives who had worked with Dubuque on Ozark, Paramount+ (Cindy Holland) and Prime HBO has greenlit a straight‑to‑series order for the Miami‑set drama starring Javier Bardem. Javier Bardem will star and executive‑produce the series Series is being co‑produced by Fifth Se
